Based on my review, I found two real issues in the onboarding flow.

**Finding 1 (medium, confidence 0.78):** `configureOnboardingEnableOptions` sets `SuppressAdditionalSetup = true`, which causes `runEnableInteractive` to skip the entire telemetry block. That block was the only place that ever wrote `settings.Telemetry = true` as the default. Everywhere `settings.Telemetry` is consumed downstream (`root.go`'s `telemetryEnabled != nil && *telemetryEnabled`, `plugin.go`'s `s.Telemetry == nil || !*s.Telemetry`, `checkpoint_policy_telemetry.go`'s same check), a `nil` value is treated as **opted out**. So every first-time user who now goes through the new default `entire configure` onboarding entry point ends up with `Telemetry: nil` persisted — silently equivalent to opting out — contradicting the documented default (`--telemetry` flag defaults to `true`, "Enable anonymous usage analytics") and diverging from the behavior of `entire enable --yes`. The stated rationale ("Login already establishes account context...") conflates authentication with the unrelated local anonymous-telemetry flag.

**Finding 2 (medium, confidence 0.7):** `configureUseMirror` reuses `planMirrorRemote`/`applyMirrorRemotePlan` from `repo_mirror_use.go` but never calls `reportMirrorRemotePlan`. That sibling function is where `preserveSkipped` gets surfaced with an explicit warning when a remote named `upstream` already exists (common on forks) — the mirror-use code calls this "the one genuinely destructive thing this command could do." In the new onboarding flow, if `upstream` is already taken, the original GitHub `origin` URL is silently discarded when `origin` is repointed to the mirror, with no warning printed anywhere.
